what: every world item pickup /map2 can honestly draw, plus the reverse index that answers "where do I get item X". Loaded LAZILY - it is not part of the map's startup payload.

inputsNotInTheRepo.what: inputs .gitignore keeps out of the checkout, digested for provenance but NOT checkable against a clean clone. Both are FMG dumps; the names they supply are in `items` already, so a change to them shows up as a diff of this file.

frame.world: worldX = px + 7040 ; worldZ = 16512 - py ; 1 master px = 1 game unit

source: regulation.bin 1.17 (bnd 11701000) -> ItemLotParam_map + ItemLotParam_enemy + ShopLineupParam(_Recipe) + EquipParamCustomWeapon + WorldMapLegacyConvParam; MSB placements from elden-ring-compass placements.ts
excluded: placements with source != 'map'. The 584 event-script placements are left out on purpose: their map attribution disagrees with the map their own pickup flag encodes in 12.9% of cases (1.8% for MSB rows), and the worst of them puts a DLC pickup 1412 px away in Stormveil.
chaining: a placement names lot L and the game rolls L, L+1, ... up to the next multiple of ten, stopping at the first missing id. `rows` is that chain and `grants` is [row, itemKey, getItemFlagId] per granted item, so a four-piece armour chest is one lot with four grants and its own flag on each row.

equipment.what: weapons, armour, talismans and ashes of war

keyAndSpells.what: key items, spirit ashes, sorceries, incantations, crystal tears, great runes, remembrances

consumables.what: every other good the world hands over - greases, boluses, throwables, cookbooks

materials.what: crafting and upgrade materials, crafting tools, ammunition

runes.what: Golden / Hero's / Lord's / Shadow Realm Runes, Rune Arcs, Broken Runes

pointFields.f: the lot's getItemFlagId - set in the save once this pickup has been taken
pointFields.l: ItemLotParam_map row id of the lot the placement names; ItemLotParam_enemy row id on a unique enemy drop (`e` present and no `a`)
pointFields.m: the map the placement lives in, for the "same map, same sheet" collapse rule
pointFields.g: which of `groups` this point draws under
pointFields.i: indices into `items` - more than one when a chest hands over a set
pointFields.ff: present only when the granted rows do not all share `f`: the per-grant flags
pointFields.e: present only on an enemy drop - a unique drop or a death award: the enemy that carries it (NpcParam names). The item is not lying there - it drops once from that one enemy
pointFields.er: Russian names for `e`, where the game has them
pointFields.a: 1 on a death award: the map's event script hands the ItemLotParam_map lot `l` over when the enemy standing here dies (scripts/maptiles/death-drops.json)
pointFields.sc: 1 when that enemy is a Teardrop Scarab. Such a point carries no `e`: the game never names scarabs, and the app says "dropped by a scarab" in the reader's language

itemFields.k: kind:id - w weapon, a armour, t talisman, e ash of war, g good
itemFields.en: English name from the game FMG, null for the three items the game never names
itemFields.ru: Russian name, null where the FMG has none
itemFields.p: indices into `points` - the reverse index. Empty means no world pickup exists
itemFields.why: present only when `p` is empty: the one reason, from `whyReasons`
itemFields.inUniverse: true if the item is one of the 2386 the collection tracker counts
itemFields.group: the group its category belongs to

whyReasons.gesture-not-a-pickup: a gesture. Not an item and never picked up - the game teaches it
whyReasons.sold-by-a-merchant: sold by a merchant. The seller is known; placing sellers on the map is separate work
whyReasons.enemy-drop: drops from enemies. A drop is not a place, so it gets no pin - unless one enemy in the whole game carries it with a one-off flag, and then it is a point (see `uniqueEnemyDrops`)
whyReasons.crafted-at-the-workbench: crafted from a recipe, not found
whyReasons.altered-at-a-grace: the "(Altered)" version of a piece you already own, made at a grace
whyReasons.awarded-by-an-event-script: awarded by an event script - a boss reward, an NPC, a quest step. Its coordinates are not trustworthy enough to draw (12.9 % disagree with the pickup flag's own map)
whyReasons.only-on-a-map-the-game-never-draws: placed only on a map the game itself never puts on the world map - the Chapel of Anticipation. The pickup is real and reachable; there is no map square to point at
whyReasons.lot-exists-but-nothing-places-it: the game has an item lot for it that nothing in the map files or the scripts we read places
whyReasons.mausoleum-duplication: obtained by duplicating a remembrance at a Walking Mausoleum
whyReasons.unused-shop-block-only: named only by a shop block with no seller - cut or debug content
whyReasons.nowhere-we-can-see: no lot, no shop, no recipe, no drop table. Either cut content or a route nothing we read describes

runes.note: not a collection category - these are the items the world hands over that the collection tracker does not track, so every one of them is here because it has a point

otherConsumables.note: not a collection category - these are the items the world hands over that the collection tracker does not track, so every one of them is here because it has a point

accounting.what: every placement the extractor offered is either a point or a dropped entry with a class, and every lot it offered is either drawn or entirely dropped. Both partitions are asserted in the build, so a silently vanished pickup fails the run instead of shipping.

uniqueEnemyDrops.what: the one-off drops of a single enemy (scripts/maptiles/unique-enemy-drops.json), grouped by flag and place. Every place is drawn, including a second place for an item a chest also hands over; `firstPlaces` counts the items that had no world point before. points + unnamed + unpainted partition `places`, first + second partition the points, and both are asserted in the build

deathDrops.what: lots the event scripts award when an enemy dies (scripts/maptiles/death-drops.json), grouped by place: one body, one point. `alreadyDrawn` are lots whose flags a point above already carries (the same lot is also a treasure on the corpse). points + alreadyDrawn + unnamed + unpainted partition `places`, first + second partition the points, and both are asserted

measurements.what: what stage 2 has to design against, measured here so the rules cannot drift from the data

mapGenieCrossCheck.what: distance in master px from each of our Scadutree Fragment / Revered Spirit Ash points to the nearest of MapGenie's hand-placed pins already on the map - the only positional evidence for this dataset that never came out of the game files. The build throws past a 40 px median.

flagCollisions.what: distinct (byte, bit) pairs the drawn pickups resolve to, counted by LOT. A collision means two different pickups grey out together, and the number is here so the UI never has to guess whether that is a bug or the game. It is small enough to ignore and too small to design around.

dropped.what: every placement this build was offered and does not draw, with a class and a reason. The classes partition `accounting.dropped` exactly.

classes.developer-placeholder: a single Rada Fruit in a DLC legacy dungeon (m20, m21): the default lot of a treasure the developers left unused, most of them parked in stacks at one coordinate. No save in the corpus has ever taken one; the two lots that were taken are kept
classes.unreachable-duplicate: a second treasure granting the same unique gear next to the real pickup, on a spot the player never reaches (Wing of Astel: the corpse below the chest near Nokstella). Drawn, it stayed "not picked up" for everyone who took the real one
classes.no-overworld-position: the legacy-dungeon conversion has no row that reaches the overworld. All of these are Chapel of Anticipation (m10_01), which the game itself never puts on a map
classes.outside-the-master-frame: projected outside the 10496 px square. Empty today
classes.unknown-sheet: routed to a sheet /map2 does not draw. Empty today
classes.unpainted-tile: landed on a z6 cell that measures as empty on its own sheet. Empty today
classes.duplicate-of-another-copy-of-the-same-ma: a LOD copy of an overworld tile, or the second state of Leyndell, placing the same lot at the same master pixel
